newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar drifts off lows by close.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar drifts off lows by close.

text.p: LIFFE white sugar futures ended slightly easier but off their lows on Tuesday ahead of the December expiry.

Most active December ended down 70 cents at $307.00 per tonne after trading between $308.00 and $305.90. Traders pegged psychological support at $300.00 but technical help could come in around $305.00.

Traders said that activity had been centred on routine trade related business in Dec/Mar switches. "It's all centred around the December expiry. People are getting out of their December longs," said one trader.
March also ended slightly weaker, down 40 cents at $305.10.
Traders said the market was debilitated by lack of significant offtake despite the recent fall in prices.
"We're talking about standard offtake," said one trader, adding that big buyers like Russia and China were absent.
In Paris, December finished down $1.90 at $305.60 and March off $1.00 at $305.00.
